A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TD-GFN work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original Hypergrid, biosequence and molecular-design experiments, including component ablations, sensitivity analyses and training-resource measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds recommendation results, further Hypergrid tests, molecular-diversity measurements and supplementary comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and Equations (4)–(7) retain the same trajectory reweighting, adversarial edge-reward extraction, pruning and prioritized backward sampling. The theoretical analysis and additional objective comparisons do not specify a revised TD-GFN procedure; soft guidance remains a future direction.

E1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds MovieLens 1M recommendation using real user-interaction trajectories to generate six-item slates. This introduces a new domain and permutation-invariant set-generation task on a general DAG, extending the retained Hypergrid, peptide and molecular-design coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds BraVE to the molecular reward and mode-discovery comparisons (Table 1 and Figure 7). Figure 19 additionally compares naive offline Dataset-GFN variants using DB, TB and SubTB objectives. These differ from v2's retained experiment applying TB within TD-GFN.

E3.justification: Added evaluation designs include ML1M user filtering, six-item slates and average/max reward and coverage metrics; a 256×256 Hypergrid with 100 training trajectories; post-hoc top-100 molecular Tanimoto similarity; and offline objective comparisons using SubTB with lambda 0.9. These supplement the retained original settings rather than establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses of widely separated Hypergrid modes, molecular structural diversity, the adequacy of naive offline GFlowNet objectives and biosequence training stability (Appendices E.3 and E.10–E.12). The earlier rebalancing, pruning, backward-sampling and threshold-sensitivity studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 0, 1 and 2 and use mean/standard-deviation reporting and shaded uncertainty bands. Best-seed reporting for molecular offline-RL baselines is retained and extended to BraVE. Additional result entries do not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports TD-GFN's ML1M average reward of 1.988±0.006 and coverage of 186.8±6.3; Table 6 adds molecular similarity of 0.531±0.022. BraVE becomes the lowest-trajectory molecular comparator at 6,450 trajectories. New Figures 10, 19 and 20 add further findings, while existing molecular reward values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 introduces Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Appendix B with formal assumptions and proofs concerning reweighting invariance, canonical-gauge reward recovery, backward-policy perturbation, pruning survival and target-distribution distortion. v2 contains background formulations and training objectives but no corresponding theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: proxy-free IRL-derived guidance, robustness through indirect use of edge rewards, faster convergence and improved sample quality. The added theory and experiments do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly treats Oracle-GFN as an online reference and qualifies canonical recovery in Remark B.6. It adds interpretations of FM robustness and soft-guidance sensitivity while removing the standalone oracle-surpassing hypotheses. Existing limitations concerning adversarial IRL, trajectory quality and continuous/stochastic extensions remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a TD-GFN source-code and reproduction-script link, ML1M construction instructions, and disclosure that biosequence baseline checkpoints were selected to balance reward and diversity. This checkpoint statement adds documentation without establishing a changed procedure. Original architecture, hyperparameter and hardware information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds BraVE (Landers et al., 2025) and FlowRL (Zhu et al., 2025), while dropping the trajectory-example references to Cobbe, Khazatsky and van der Kamp. The substantive related-work discussion is largely retained; several other citation changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the main-text prose are extensively rewritten, and the introductory motivation is reorganized. Appendix organization changes around the new theory section, the supplementary contents page disappears, and the discussions are revised. This exceeds simple renumbering or additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout. Hypergrid panels are redistributed, the biosequence chart becomes vertically arranged, and the pipeline diagram is redrawn. v2's introductory summary plot is removed, new tables and figures are added, and Table 1 visually separates reference methods from offline comparators.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens justification and validation: Appendix B supplies explicit conditions and proofs, while ML1M extends real-data evidence beyond v2's tree-structured peptide task to user trajectories in a general DAG. Added diversity and stability analyses and clearer comparison disclosures improve scrutiny. The guarantees remain conditional, and Section 4.1's DB/SubTB compatibility assertion lacks corresponding results in Appendix E.8, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains.
